title: Trump's six-day denial flip: G7 'mistake' admission vs Oval Office 'I don't think it was us' on the Minab school strike that killed 168 children
deck: Pentagon's internal finding says US forces were likely responsible — for a Tomahawk fired on a girls' elementary school at coordinates a CENTCOM officer pulled from an outdated DIA target package. The 'elevated' investigation has now been frozen for 16 weeks.
narrative:
On Wednesday June 24 2026, in the Oval Office beside Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, President Donald Trump told reporters that 'fault' for the February 28 Tomahawk strike on the Shaid Hasheminejad girls' elementary school in Minab, southern Iran, **'may never be known.'** 'I don't know that they are ever going to solve that problem in terms of whose fault was it because there were missiles flying all over the place,' Trump said. 'Somebody said it was our missile, maybe it wasn't our missile but I have seen nothing to lead me to believe it was. I don't think it was us.' Hegseth, seated on a couch, added: 'Mr President, we've taken the investigation very seriously, and when the appropriate time is right, whatever that outcome is, that'll be the time to divulge.'

The Hill (Ashleigh Fields, June 25) provides the physical-evidence chain. The strike killed **175 people, 168 of them children aged 7-12.** An initial internal US military investigation reported by Reuters in March — and since 'elevated' by the Pentagon — concluded that **US forces were likely responsible** because CENTCOM officers used **outdated and unverified target coordinates** provided by the Defense Intelligence Agency for a nearby Iranian base. The base 'had once extended onto the school grounds, which had since been designated as a civilian area (marked with a wall and bright painted colors).'

South China Morning Post (June 25, Reuters wire) confirms: 'Reuters first reported in March that an initial internal US military investigation showed US forces were likely responsible for the fatal strike in Minab in southern Iran. The Pentagon has since elevated the probe but **has not acknowledged any preliminary findings.**' Hindustan Times adds that Trump, at the G7 summit in France **last week**, 'acknowledged that Minab school strikes were a 'mistake' and was not intentional' — meaning the Oval Office 'I don't think it was us' formulation now contradicts the on-record G7 acknowledgment Trump himself made six days earlier.
research:
**1. The internal investigation chain — and what 'elevated' means.** Reuters reported in March 2026 that an initial internal military investigation showed US forces were likely responsible. The Pentagon's response has been to 'elevate' the probe (a procedural step) — which does NOT mean the conclusion has changed. Pentagon has 'not acknowledged any preliminary findings' because acknowledging them would convert the elevated review from an internal fact-finding exercise into an admission that grounds a domestic and international legal liability chain. The procedural elevation is the structural reason the school-strike investigation has been frozen for ~16 weeks despite an existing preliminary US-responsibility finding.

**2. The targeting data — AI + outdated DIA coordinates.** The Hill writeup reconstructs the chain: DIA-provided target coordinates for a 'nearby Iranian base' → CENTCOM used those coordinates → the base 'had once extended onto the school grounds' → the school 'had since been designated as a civilian area (marked with a wall and bright painted colors)' → Tomahawk strike on coordinates. The Senate Democrats' letter specifically references the 'reported use of artificial intelligence tools to select and prioritize targets' — meaning the AI-tooling aspect is on-record in a congressional document, not speculative.

**3. Trump's six-day contradiction between G7 and Oval Office.** Hindustan Times: 'Donald Trump last week at G7 summit in France acknowledged that Minab school strikes were a 'mistake' and was not intentional.' Six days later, in the Oval Office beside Hegseth: 'I don't think it was us.' These are not reconcilable. The G7 acknowledgment creates a documented prior admission; the Oval Office denial creates a documented current denial. The 'missiles flying all over the place' framing is the structural alibi — it dissolves attribution into chaos rather than naming the Tomahawk source, which the preliminary finding already does.

**4. Hegseth's 'when the appropriate time is right' formulation.** Hegseth's answer is the procedural-recusation pattern: deflect to 'the appropriate time' rather than address the substance. It permits indefinite deferral of the conclusion while leaving the legal exposure path open. The structural effect is to convert an existing internal finding into a perpetually-pending investigation.

**5. The 168-children number as the structural reason no one wants the conclusion on the record.** 168 children aged 7-12 killed is the catastrophic-civilian-casualty threshold that, under the Law of Armed Conflict principles of distinction and proportionality, converts a strike into a war-crime exposure for the chain of command. The structural reason no entity — Trump, Hegseth, the Pentagon — wants the preliminary 'US responsibility' finding acknowledged is that acknowledgment activates the legal liability chain. Hegseth's 'appropriate time' formulation is functionally a liability-gate deferral.

**6. The AI-targeting-tools component.** The Senate Democrats' letter to Hegseth is the congressional-record anchor for the AI-targeting dimension. It specifies the 'reported use of artificial intelligence tools to select and prioritize targets in Iran' — meaning the AI toolset is named in an official communication to the Secretary of Defense, not in speculative reporting. The combination of outdated human-curated DIA coordinates + an AI-targeting pipeline is the structural reason a school got a Tomahawk — and the structural reason no one in the chain of command wants the post-strike fact pattern admitted.

**7. Timeline:**
- **Feb 28 2026:** Strike on Minab girls' school (Day 1 of US-Israel war on Iran).
- **March 2026:** Reuters reports preliminary internal US finding. Senate Democrats send letter to Hegseth.
- **March 2026 onward:** Pentagon 'elevates' the probe, no preliminary findings acknowledged.
- **~June 18-19 2026:** Trump tells G7 (France) the strike was a 'mistake' and not intentional.
- **June 24 2026 (Wednesday):** Trump in Oval Office beside Hegseth: 'I don't think it was us'; 'fault may never be known.' Hegseth: 'when the appropriate time is right.'
analysis:
The structural pattern here is not a denial — it is a denial that *contradicts the denier's own prior admission.* Trump told the G7 in France that the strike was a 'mistake.' Six days later, in the Oval Office beside the Secretary of Defense, he told the American public 'I don't think it was us.' Both statements are on the public record. The G7 statement creates a documented prior admission of fault; the Oval Office statement creates a documented current denial. Neither party to the contradiction has retracted the other. The contradiction is the load-bearing finding.

The Pentagon's 'elevated the probe' formulation is the procedural-language cover. 'Elevated' is a procedural step that signals gravity without signaling new content. It permits the agency to acknowledge that the investigation matters without acknowledging what the investigation has found. The fact that 16 weeks have elapsed since the preliminary finding without any acknowledgment of preliminary findings is itself evidence: if the elevated review had reversed the preliminary finding, the conclusion would have been published to support the Oval Office denial. The fact that it has not been published is consistent with the preliminary finding standing.

The 168-children figure is the structural reason for the freeze. Under the Law of Armed Conflict — the customary international legal regime that governs targeting decisions — the principles of distinction (combatants vs civilians) and proportionality (expected civilian harm vs military advantage) are the operative tests. A strike that kills 168 children at a girls' elementary school fails both tests on the face of the public record. The chain of command exposure runs from the targeting officer who selected the coordinates, to the DIA analyst who provided them, to the CENTCOM commander who approved the strike, to the Secretary of Defense, to the Commander-in-Chief. Hegseth's 'appropriate time' formulation is functionally a liability-gate deferral — it converts the question 'what did the targeting system produce?' into 'when will we deign to answer?'

The AI-targeting dimension is the structural reason the contradiction has to stay open. If the post-strike finding were published, it would document the failure of an AI-assisted targeting pipeline on a school. That failure would have to be addressed not only for the Minab strike but for the broader Iran-war targeting campaign — which used AI tools to select and prioritize targets at scale. The Senate Democrats' letter is the congressional-record anchor that says the AI-targeting question is already on the formal oversight docket. Hegseth cannot publish a finding that admits the AI pipeline produced a school-strike without admitting the AI pipeline's broader targeting outputs are also under legal scrutiny.

The Minab strike is the structural reason the US has refused to publish its own internal finding 16 weeks later. The Oval Office 'I don't think it was us' formulation is not a counter-claim grounded in evidence — it is a counter-claim grounded in deferral. Trump is not asserting a positive alternative attribution; he is asserting that fault 'may never be known' and that 'there were missiles flying all over the place.' The structural alibi dissolves the attribution question into chaos rather than naming the Tomahawk source, which the preliminary finding already does.
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: The Minab school strike is the structural test of whether the US government will acknowledge — on the public record — that its own internal investigation has produced a finding. Sixteen weeks in, it has not. The 'elevated' investigation has not been published, the preliminary 'US forces were likely responsible' finding has not been retracted, and the Oval Office denial posture has not been reconciled with Trump's own G7 'mistake' admission six days earlier. Hegseth's 'appropriate time' formulation is the procedural-recusation pattern that converts an existing internal finding into a perpetually-pending question. The 168-children civilian-casualty count is the structural reason the question cannot be resolved: an acknowledgment of US responsibility activates the Law of Armed Command liability chain for distinction and proportionality failures across the entire AI-assisted targeting campaign. The Minab strike is the case the Pentagon cannot afford to admit — and the Oval Office denial is the rhetorical posture that permits the deferral to continue without the cost of a public retraction of the G7 admission. The contradiction is not noise. It is the operational state.
